cells.tense: You're at the bench and you know exactly why you're there — the work is deepening and you can feel it deepening.
cells.ask: Let this stretch feed the next layer of skill: take one practice you've been repeating and refine it a notch past where it's comfortable.
cells.core:
You're standing back far enough to see the whole shape, and you're still in the room it lives in. The pattern shows itself because you've stayed with it long enough — through reps that weren't exciting, through the middle stretch nobody claps for.

Someone asks how you did it and the honest answer is: kept showing up, and looked at what was actually there. The room is steady, the reps are steady, and the seeing has gotten sharp because the making never stopped. That's the thing to feed now. Take one piece of what you've built and sharpen it rather than widen it — the depth is the point, and the seeing and the making are the same act.
cells.sheetLine: You see the whole shape because you stayed long enough to earn the view.
cells.verb: committing to the long, deep build — the patient craft that only time at the bench can make
cells.place: standing back far enough to see the whole shape without leaving the room it lives in

cells.tense: You're already at the end of the build in your head — finished, proven, past the part where it could still go wrong.
cells.ask: Step out of the alone-with-it and put the work where it can be met: one showing, one person, one room that didn't ask for a masterpiece — just something to touch and respond to.
cells.core:
You're standing back to see the pattern and what you see is the version that's finished — the one ahead, the one where it all locks in. So the present build reads as pre-work, and you keep racing it, because the only way to live in that future is to get there faster than the work actually goes.

That vision tells you what the thing could be, which is real information. It also cuts you off from the only place the thing gets made — the slow middle, where it's still soft and could be talked to. Take it off the workbench. Let one person who cares about the thing look at the thing and say what they see, before it's finished. The build is meant to belong somewhere, and the belonging isn't a reward at the end. It's part of how the thing gets made.
cells.sheetLine: You're racing toward a finished version only you can picture.

cells.tense: You can still picture the bench, the practice, the long build — but that picture is behind you now, and you haven't stepped back to the work in a while.
cells.ask: Declare what you're making — to one person, in plain words. Not a report on progress; a statement of what you're building and why it matters. Put structure around the thing so you have somewhere to stand.
cells.core:
You're standing back far enough to see the shape and the shape has gone quiet — you used to know why the reps mattered and now the reps are just reps. Not because the skill left. Because the longer view went missing, and without it the work stopped feeling like it was going somewhere.

This isn't a dry spell in the craft; it's a gap where the big picture should be. Say the thing out loud. Not to justify it — to name it. 'I'm building this, and here's the pattern it's part of.' A structure you've put into words is a structure you can stand in again. The seeing comes back when the making has a claim on it.
cells.sheetLine: You lost sight of the shape and the daily work stopped reaching you.

cells.tense: You're already doing the seeing — you clock the pattern in the room while everyone's still arguing about details — but you haven't let yourself call it yours.
cells.ask: Let the pattern you see move you before you've figured out how to use it: one honest response to what's in front of you — your actual read — given before you've decided it's strategic.
cells.core:
You're standing back and reading the whole shape — it's happening, you're doing it — but the read gets filed as the room's information rather than your perception. The seeing runs; the ownership of it doesn't.

The move here is smaller than the read. Somewhere under the long build there's a reason you started — something that pulled you, before it became a thing you do. Let that have a say. Not a plan, not a strategy: one motion that comes from genuine engagement rather than the finished structure you've been maintaining. The direction has a source. Touch it and the whole thing moves again.
cells.sheetLine: You're reading the room — the read just isn't claimed as yours.
